producer: Media Exchange Server (Go) of Fast Media Sorter & Sharing for Windows, cmd/exchange-vectors
notes: Every transcript was produced by the real exchange server (engine, directory, accounts, relay, cast table) over TLS on loopback, with one injected clock instant, seeded id and token sources and a third-party port pool whose binds are not sockets. The bytes are a function of the code and nothing else.

A step is one frame as it crossed the stream above TLS: `json` is the body, `hex` is the whole frame (the 4-byte big-endian length, then the body). A frame is recorded when the script reads or writes it, in the order of the script.

A client replays a transcript by encoding every client->server step to exactly its `hex` and decoding every server->client step to the same values. Ids, tokens and codes are the scenario's; a client under test supplies its own ids and compares the rest.

After `connected` and after `upload-accepted` the bytes are not envelopes: tunnels are recorded up to `connected` and never beyond; an upload continues as `chunk` steps (a 4-byte length counting the flag byte plus the payload, the flag byte, the payload) and the listener's HTTP exchange is an `http` step.

`chunks` lists every flag combination of the two defined bits, a zero length (the clean end of a broadcast) and the chunks that close a stream (an undefined flag bit, a length above 1048576, the largest length word); a chunk of exactly 1048576 bytes of length is the largest accepted and is not listed because of its size.
The frame limit is 16384 bytes of JSON until a stream is authenticated (up to and including welcome or enrolled) and 262144 after it, both ways; a record is at most 16384 bytes of JSON.

Reasons: bad-credentials, device-revoked, version-unsupported, tls-required, id-collision, capacity, port-unavailable, unavailable and rate-limited are all produced in the `refusals` transcript; the refusal that answers a schemaVersion 1 frame carries schemaVersion 2.

transcripts.name: refusals
transcripts.description: Every refusal reason of DEVICE-EXCHANGE 7.10 produced by the real server: tls-required and version-unsupported on a plain stream, id-collision, capacity, port-unavailable, unavailable, device-revoked, bad-credentials and rate-limited. The failed-authentication bucket of this server holds 2 and does not refill during the run, so the last three steps are the ones that spend it.

transcripts.name: tunnels
transcripts.description: A consumer opens a data stream and says connect; the server sends the producer open on its control stream; the producer opens a new data stream, says hello and attach; the server answers the consumer connected and splices the two. After connected nothing is an envelope: the transcript stops there.

transcripts.name: relay
transcripts.description: The fan-out relay: the broadcaster starts a broadcast, opens a data stream, says upload and receives upload-accepted; from then on the stream carries chunks (a 4-byte length counting one flag byte plus the payload, the flag byte, the payload; a length of zero ends the broadcast). A listener GETs /v2/b/<broadcastId>/stream inside TLS and receives the header chunk and then the stream from a joinable chunk.

transcripts.name: cast
transcripts.description: Cast: a device asks one named receiver of the same account to play a broadcast. The server forwards cast-offer to the receiver (the broadcast record, never access), the receiver's cast-answer to the caster as cast-result, and cast-stop to the other end. An offline receiver is answered at once; a receiver that does not answer in 60 s is a timeout.
